en: Thus have I heard— The Shorter Exposition of Kamma (Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasutta), Discourse 135 of the Majjhima Nikāya.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then the brahmin student Subha, the son of Todeyya, approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
When they had concluded their polite and courteous conversation, he sat down to one side. Sitting there, the brahmin student Subha, the son of Todeyya, said this to the Blessed One:
“Master Gotama, what is the cause, what is the reason why, among those who are human beings, humans are seen to be both inferior and superior?
For, Master Gotama, some humans are seen to be short-lived, while others are seen to be long-lived;
some are seen to be afflicted with many ailments, while others are seen to be free from many ailments.”
Some are seen who are ugly, some who are beautiful;
some are seen who have little influence, some who have great influence;
some are seen who have little wealth, some who have great wealth.
"We see those born of low families, and we see those born of high families;
we see those who are witless, and we see those who possess wisdom.
What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason why, among those who are merely human beings, such inferiority and excellence are seen?"
“Students, beings are owners of their actions, heirs of their actions; they originate from their actions, are bound to their actions, and have their actions as their refuge.
It is action that divides beings into the inferior and the superior.”
“I do not understand the detailed meaning of this brief statement made by Master Gotama, which has not been explained in detail.
It would be well if Master Gotama would teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might understand the detailed meaning of this brief statement made by him, which has not been explained in detail.
“In that case, young man, listen and pay close attention; I shall speak.”
“Yes, sir,” the young brahmin Subha, son of Todeyya, replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“In this case, young man, some woman or man is a destroyer of life—cruel, bloody-handed, devoted to killing and striking, and lacking compassion for living beings.”
Thus, by having performed and undertaken such an action, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.

But if, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or in hell, and instead returns to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one is short-lived.
This, young man, is the practice that leads to a short life; that is to say: [the aforementioned actions].
He is a destroyer of life, cruel, with blood on his hands, devoted to killing and slaughtering, and devoid of compassion for living beings.

But here, young man, some woman or man, having abandoned the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life; he lays aside the rod and the weapon, and being modest and compassionate, he dwells sympathetic toward the welfare of all living beings.
By that action, so performed and so undertaken, upon the breakup of the body after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in a heavenly world.
If, with the breakup of the body after death, he does not reappear in a happy destination, in a heavenly world, but returns to the human state, wherever he is reborn, he will be long-lived.
This, young man, is the practice that leads to longevity:

namely, having abandoned the taking of life, he abstains from taking life; he lays aside the rod and the sword, and dwells conscientious and compassionate, sympathetic toward the welfare of all living beings.
In this case, student, a certain woman or man is by nature a harasser of living beings, using his hand, a clod of earth, a staff, or a sword.
By that action, so performed and so undertaken, with the breakup of the body after death, he is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.

But if, with the breakup of the body after death, he is not reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or in hell, and instead returns to the human state, wherever he is reborn, he will be afflicted with much illness.
"This practice, young man, leads to much affliction:
namely, when one is habitually inclined to harm living beings with the hand, with a clod, with a staff, or with a weapon.
But here, young man, some woman or man is not habitually inclined to harm living beings with the hand, with a clod, with a staff, or with a weapon."
Thus, by having fulfilled and undertaken that kamma, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

But if, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world, and instead comes back to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one is free from illness. This practice, young man, leads to freedom from illness; that is to say: [The following verses follow: One who is skilled in wholesome qualities, Who is wise and endowed with faith, Having performed such deeds as these, Is reborn in heaven, a place of bliss. But if, having passed away from there, One returns to the human state, Wherever one is reborn, One is free from illness.
This, young man, is the path that leads to freedom from illness, namely: [The preceding verse].”
He is by nature non-violent toward living beings, whether with his hand, a clod of earth, a staff, or a sword.
Here, young man, a certain woman or man is prone to anger and full of vexation;
even when spoken to only slightly, he becomes resentful, agitated, malicious, and stubborn, manifesting anger, hatred, and resentment.
Thus, by having fulfilled and undertaken that kamma, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.

But if, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or in hell, and instead returns to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one is ugly.
This, young man, is the practice that leads to ugliness, namely: [the aforementioned unwholesome deeds].
He is prone to anger and full of distress;
even when addressed with only a little, he becomes resentful, agitated, and ill-tempered, becoming stubborn and manifesting anger, hatred, and resentment.
But here, young man, a certain woman or man is not prone to anger and is not full of distress.

Even when addressed with much [harshness], he does not become resentful, does not become angry, does not harbor ill will, does not remain fixed in resentment, and does not manifest anger, hatred, or dissatisfaction.
Because of that action—having been thus completed and thus undertaken—upon the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a happy destination, in a heavenly world.
If, upon the breakup of the body, after death, he is not reborn in a happy destination, in a heavenly world, but returns to the human state, wherever he is reborn, he is pleasing to behold.
This is the practice leading to serenity, student:
namely, that one is free from anger and largely devoid of distress;
even when spoken to much, one does not become resentful, does not become angry, does not harbor ill will, does not remain obstinate, and does not manifest anger, hatred, or resentment.
In this case, student, a certain woman or man is envious;
he envies, resents, and harbors envy regarding the gains, honors, respect, esteem, veneration, and offerings received by others.
By that action, thus performed and thus undertaken, with the breakup of the body after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower world, even in hell.

If, with the breakup of the body after death, he does not reappear in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or in hell, but instead returns to the human state, wherever he is reborn, he will be of little influence.
This practice, student, leads to being of little influence, namely:
being envious.
One envies, becomes ill-willed toward, and harbors envy regarding the gains, honors, respect, esteem, veneration, and worship received by others.
But here, student, some woman or man is not envious;
they do not envy, become ill-willed toward, or harbor envy regarding the gains, honors, respect, esteem, veneration, and worship received by others.
Thus, by having fulfilled and undertaken that kamma, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

If, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world, but instead returns to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one becomes highly influential.
This, young man, is the practice that leads to being highly influential, namely: [the aforementioned deeds].
He is not envious;
he does not envy, does not become ill-willed toward, and does not harbor envy regarding the gains, honors, respect, esteem, veneration, and worship accorded to others.
In this case, student, a certain woman or man is not a giver of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, bedding, dwellings, or lamps to a recluse or a brahmin.
Thus, by having fulfilled and undertaken that kamma, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower world, or hell.

But if, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower world, or hell, and instead returns to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one is of little wealth.
This, young man, is the practice that leads to being of little wealth, namely: [the aforementioned unwholesome conduct].
He does not give food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, bedding, dwellings, or lamps to a recluse or a brahmin.
But here, young man, some woman or man is a giver of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, bedding, dwellings, and lamps to a recluse or a brahmin.
By that karma, so performed and so undertaken, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a happy destination, in a heavenly world.
If, with the breakup of the body after death, one does not reappear in a happy destination, a heavenly world, but returns to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one becomes very wealthy.
This, young man, is the practice that leads to great wealth:
namely, being a giver of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, beds, dwellings, and lamps to ascetics or brahmins.
In this case, student, some woman or man is stubborn and conceited:
he does not salute one who should be saluted; he does not rise for one who should be risen for; he does not offer a seat to one worthy of a seat;
he does not yield the path to one worthy of the path; he does not honor one who should be honored; he does not respect one who should be respected.
He does not honor those who should be honored; he does not revere those who should be revered.
Because of that action, so performed and so undertaken, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

If, however, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is not reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or hell, but instead returns to the human state, wherever he is reborn, he is born into a low family.
"Student, this practice leads to birth in a low family:
namely, one is stubborn and conceited;
one does not pay homage to those who should be saluted, one does not rise for those who should be stood up for, and one does not offer a seat to one who deserves a seat."
He does not give [what is due]; he does not give the path to one who deserves the path; he does not honor one who should be honored;
he does not revere one who should be revered; he does not respect one who should be respected; he does not worship one who should be worshipped.
But here, student, a certain woman or man is free from arrogance and free from conceit.
One who should be saluted, he salutes; one who should be risen for, he rises for; to one worthy of a seat, he gives a seat;
to one worthy of the path, he gives way; one who should be honored, he honors; one who should be revered, he reveres; one who should be respected, he respects;
one who should be venerated, he venerates.

Thus, by that very action having been performed and undertaken in such a way, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. If, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world, but instead comes to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one is born into a high family. This, young man, is the practice that leads to being born into a high family; that is to say: [The following verses follow: “By what kind of deeds does one become wealthy? By what kind of deeds does one become poor? By what kind of deeds does one become wise? By what kind of deeds does one become dull-witted? “By deeds of giving one becomes wealthy; By deeds of stinginess one becomes poor. By deeds of wisdom one becomes wise; By deeds of ignorance one becomes dull-witted. “By what kind of deeds does one become long-lived? By what kind of deeds does one become short-lived? By what kind of deeds does one become sickly? By what kind of deeds does one become healthy? “By deeds of non-harming one becomes long-lived; By deeds of harming one becomes short-lived. By deeds of cruelty one becomes sickly; By deeds of kindness one becomes healthy. “By what kind of deeds does one become ugly? By what kind of deeds does one become beautiful? By what kind of deeds does one become weak? By what kind of deeds does one become powerful? “By deeds of anger one becomes ugly; By deeds of patience one becomes beautiful. By deeds of violence one becomes weak; By deeds of gentleness one becomes powerful. “By what kind of deeds does one become low-born? By what kind of deeds does one become high-born? By what kind of deeds does one become influential? By what kind of deeds does one become powerless? “By deeds of pride one becomes low-born; By deeds of humility one becomes high-born. By deeds of influence one becomes influential; By deeds of subservience one becomes powerless. “By what kind of deeds does one become a fool? By what kind of deeds does one become a sage? By what kind of deeds does one become a beast? By what kind of deeds does one become a god?

“By deeds of heedlessness one becomes a fool; By deeds of heedfulness one becomes a sage. By deeds of cruelty one becomes a beast; By deeds of virtue one becomes a god. “This, young man, is the practice that leads to being born into a high family; that is to say: [and so forth].
He is free from stubbornness and is without arrogance;
he salutes one who should be saluted, rises for one who should be risen for, gives a seat to one worthy of a seat,
gives way to one worthy of way, honors one worthy of honor, reveres one worthy of reverence, and respects one worthy of respect.
He honors what is worthy of honor.
Here, student, a certain woman or man, having approached a recluse or a brahmin, does not inquire:
“Venerable sir, what is wholesome? What is unwholesome?”
‘What is blameworthy? What is blameless?
What should be cultivated? What should not be cultivated?
What, when done by me, will lead to long-term harm and suffering? Or what, when done by me, will lead to long-term welfare and happiness?’”
Thus, by having performed and undertaken such an action, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.

But if, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or in hell, and instead returns to the human state, wherever one is reborn, one is dull-witted.
This practice, student, leads to dullness of wit; that is to say: [the aforementioned action].
Having approached a recluse or a brahmin, she does not inquire:
"Venerable sir, what is wholesome? What is unwholesome?
What is blameworthy? What is blameless?"
‘What should be cultivated? What should not be cultivated?
What, when done by me, leads to harm and suffering for a long time? Or what, when done by me, leads to welfare and happiness for a long time?
But here, student, a certain woman or man approaches a recluse or a brahmin and asks:
“Venerable sir, what is wholesome? What is unwholesome?
What is blameworthy? What is blameless?
What should be cultivated? What should not be cultivated?”
‘What action being performed by me will lead to my harm and suffering for a long time? Or what action being performed by me will lead to my welfare and happiness for a long time?
Because he has fully completed and undertaken that action, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.
If, however, he is not reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world, but returns to the human state, wherever he is reborn, he is of great wisdom.
This, young man, is the practice conducive to great wisdom:
namely, approaching a recluse or a brahmin and inquiring:
“What, venerable sir, is wholesome? What is unwholesome?”
‘What is blameworthy? What is blameless?
What should be cultivated? What should not be cultivated?
What, when done by me, will lead to long-term harm and suffering? Or what, when done by me, will lead to long-term welfare and happiness?’”
Thus, young man, the practice leading to a short life brings about a short life; the practice leading to a long life brings about a long life.
The practice leading to much illness brings about much illness; the practice leading to little illness brings about little illness.
The practice leading to ugliness brings about ugliness; the practice leading to beauty brings about beauty.
The practice leading to lack of influence brings about lack of influence; the practice leading to great influence brings about great influence.
The practice leading to lack of wealth brings about lack of wealth; the practice leading to great wealth brings about great wealth.
The practice leading to birth in a low family brings about birth in a low family; the practice leading to birth in a high family brings about birth in a high family.
The practice leading to lack of wisdom brings one to a state of lack of wisdom; the practice leading to great wisdom brings one to a state of great wisdom.
Students, beings are owners of their actions, heirs of their actions, born of their actions, bound to their actions, and have their actions as their refuge.
It is action that divides beings, namely:
“...due to inferiority and superiority.
When this was said, the young brahmin Subha, the son of Todeyya, said to the Blessed One:
“Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama!”
"Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden,
or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—
even so has the Dhamma been made clear by Master Gotama in many ways."
“I go for refuge to Master Gotama, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
May Master Gotama accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.
The Shorter Exposition of Kamma Sutta is finished; it is the fifth.
